# Q1: Using their unique donor IDs, how many patients appear across all four arms of the study?

## 1. Load and inspect datasets

```{r}
# Load tidyverse for data manipulation
library(tidyverse)

# Import datasets from all four study arms
load("data/prs.Rda")
load("data/rnaseq.Rda")
load("data/drugscreen.Rda")
load("data/gait.Rda")
```

```{r}
# Inspect donor IDs in each dataset to determine 
# whether patients can be matched 

# Check population genetics donor IDs
head(ca_co_genotypes$donorid)

# Check RNA-seq sample information
head(dge$samples)
colnames(dge$samples)
rownames(dge$samples)

# Check clinical trial donor IDs
head(gait_data$donorid)

# Check drug screening metadata
colnames(plate_meta)
colnames(compound_dict)
```

## 2. Extract unique donor IDs

```{r}
# Extract unique donor IDs from population genetics
prs_ids <- ca_co_genotypes |> 
  distinct(donorid)

# Extract unique donor IDS from RNAseq sample metadata
rna_ids <- dge$samples |> 
  distinct(donorid) 

# Extract unique donor IDs from clinical trial data
gait_ids <- gait_data |> 
  distinct(donorid)
```

## 3. Identify overlapping patients

# Count the number of unique overlapping donors

n_overlapping <- length(overlapping_donors)

```{r}
# Identify unique donor IDs present in all three datasets
# intersect() automatically removes duplicate values
# Reduce() applies intersect() successively across the datasets

overlapping_donors <- Reduce(
  intersect,
  list(
    ca_co_genotypes$donorid,
    dge$samples$donorid,
    gait_data$donorid
  )
)

# Exclude missing donor IDs
overlapping_donors <- overlapping_donors[!is.na(overlapping_donors)]

# Display shared donor IDs
knitr::kable(overlapping_donors)

# Count the number of unique overlapping donors
length(overlapping_donors) 
```

## 4. Results and Interpretation

Using the unique donor IDs, we identified 8 participants who appeared in the population genetics, RNA-seq and clinical trial datasets. However, the drug screening dataset did not provide identifiable donor IDs for matching with the other datasets. Therefore, although 8 participants were confirmed to overlap across three study arms, the number of participants appearing across all four arms could not be determined from the available donor information.
